subject: Acme POC kickoff \u0014 scope, success metrics, access & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC kickoff  scope, success metrics, access & next steps

Hi Jordan  great to meet earlier. Thanks for the detailed walkthrough of Acme's support summarization use case. Per our call, below is a concise recap and proposed kickoff plan so we have clear owners and timelines. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

Goal (why):
- Reduce manual triage time for support agents by surfacing concise, accurate summaries and suggested tags for incoming tickets.
- Target outcomes: 30% reduction in average handling time (AHT) and 20% fewer escalations within 90 days.

Primary pain points you shared:
- Current model latency spikes during peak hours causing timeouts in the UI (observed spikes to 700900ms).
- Cost unpredictability due to variable batching and infrastructure overhead.
- Need for data isolation and SOC2 evidence for the pilot (some tickets contain PII).

Success metrics for the POC (agreed):
- 95th percentile generation latency <= 150ms for short summaries (<= 512 tokens) under a 100 qps sustained load.
- Token cost <= $0.0008/token equivalent for inference during pilot (target).
- Summary accuracy: >85% of summaries rated acceptable/usable by agents in prompt-set evaluation.

Proposed scope (4 weeks POC):
- Week 0-1: Access & data prep  service account + sample prompt set (you provide 500 anonymized tickets), IP allowlist + audit evidence.
- Week 1-2: Integration + model mapping  Redwood provides a test endpoint (dedicated pool) and sample prompt templates; solutions eng to tune prompt set and batching.
- Week 2-3: Eval & iterations  run automated evals on the prompt set, collect agent feedback, measure latency and cost.
- Week 4: Final review & recommendations  shared report (latency/cost/quality) and rollout plan.

Owners:
- Acme: Jordan Ellis (Product / POC lead), Priya Shah (Engineering lead), ACME IT for networking.
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, program lead), Rishi Malhotra (Solutions Engineering, tuning + infra), Aditya Rao (Security/compliance point).

Immediate next steps (today / this week):
1) Jordan / Priya: confirm sample dataset delivery timeline (500 tickets, anonymized) and provide an owner for IT networking.
2) ACME IT: add the following outbound allowlist IPs and confirm VPN/KMS requirements  instructions in attached redwood_access_instructions.md.
3) Redwood: share POC scope document and mutual action plan (attached). Rishi will reach out to schedule a 60-minute integration session.

Attachments: acme_poc_scope_v1.pdf, redwood_access_instructions.md, acme_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

If that all looks right, we'll schedule the integration session for next Tue or Wed (your preference).

Thanks  excited to get started.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0118

References: internal follow-ups will include perf targets and prompt-set eval templates.

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, ACME IT <it@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC kickoff  scope, success metrics, access & next steps

Thanks Marissa  this is excellent and lines up with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications and asks: 

1) Dataset: we can deliver the 500 anonymized tickets by end of day Friday (I'll have Priya confirm). They will be in CSV with ticket_id, subject, body, and agent_feedback columns. Is that format okay?

2) Latency SLA: the 95th <=150ms target is ambitious; can you confirm whether that is for p99 on single-token generation or for end-to-end response including network hop? We need to map against our UI UX budget.

3) Security: ACME requires SOC2 evidence and an encrypted transit path. Aditya / Redwood: can you confirm the timeline for providing SOC2 docs and whether we can integrate with our KMS (AWS KMS) for the duration of the pilot?

4) Integration session: Tuesday (27 Jul) at 11:00am PT works for our team  please send an invite.

We'll get the dataset ready and have IT review the access doc you attached.

Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
jordan.ellis@acme.com
+1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, ACME IT <it@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC kickoff  scope, success metrics, access & next steps

Thanks Jordan  quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) Dataset format: CSV with the fields you listed is perfect. Please remove any direct PII; if you want, we can run a quick scrub script on our side once you upload to the shared drive.

2) Latency target clarification: the 95th <=150ms target refers to end-to-end server-side generation time (model inference + Redwood runtime processing) measured at the Redwood endpoint under a 100 qps sustained synthetic load. Network hop/UI rendering is separate  if you need p95 end-to-end including network, let's add ~2550ms buffer. Rishi will include measurement details in the eval plan.

3) Security / SOC2 / KMS: Aditya  can you confirm SOC2 evidence availability and KMS options?

Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Jordan / Priya  we can provide SOC2 Type II report and our security questionnaire within 48 hours. For the pilot we support AWS KMS integration for key wrap; we'll send the integration checklist and expected timelines (typically 35 business days for the config + test).

4) Integration session invite: scheduled for Tue, 27 Jul 2027 at 11:00 AM PT. Calendar invite sent. Rishi will lead the session and will bring tuning checklist and prompt templates.

Action items (owners):
- Jordan / Priya (Acme): upload anonymized CSV to the shared Drive by EOD Fri (23 Jul).
- ACME IT: review redwood_access_instructions.md and confirm IP allowlist / KMS needs (cc'ed).
- Aditya (Redwood): send SOC2 evidence + KMS integration checklist (by 25 Jul).
- Rishi (Redwood): follow up with prompt-set eval plan and measurement scripts (by 26 Jul).

I've attached the latest POC scope (acme_poc_scope_v1.pdf) and the mutual action plan  please review and we'll incorporate any edits.

Appreciate the quick turnaround  we'll aim to have the system live in test by the end of week 2 so you can begin agent evaluations.

Best,
Marissa
